author: Jack Batten
title: South Gwinnett cruises past Lanier in Georgia's 1st regular-season football game - NewsBreak
text:
By Jack Batten ,
1 hours ago South Gwinnett quarterback C.J. Peoples (7) passes during the Corky Kell + Dave Hunter Classic football showcase at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta on August 12, 2026. By Dale Zanine ATLANTA — South Gwinnett head coach Bryan Lamar didn’t mind the fact that his team was on display in the continental United States’ first high school football game of the year.
Even better that way, in fact.
“I liked the early start because our kids struggle with downtime,” Lamar said with a smile after the Comets’ 29-3 dismantling of Lanier in Wednesday’s Corky Kell + Dave Hunter Classic. “So getting them out of class and getting them down here, that was perfect for our group.”
South didn’t struggle with much at all at Mercedes-Benz Stadium Wednesday. C.J. Peoples threw for 103 yards and a touchdown, and ran for 42 yards and a score, while a stout Comet defense — led by Jay Medlock’s 10 tackles — had 10 tackles for loss in a dominating performance.
Even 20 penalties for 167 yards didn’t seem to matter in the season opener — although they were at the forefront of Lamar’s mind afterward.
“We shot ourselves in the foot so many times,” Lamar said. “We didn't play anywhere near as clean a game as we wanted to. We’ve got high expectations for our group and we’ve got to get to practicing. It's an early start to the season, so we’ve got to get out next week and get some work done.”
On the other sideline, almost nothing went right. Lanier turned the ball over twice, rushed for only 70 yards and converted just 3 of 13 third downs. The Longhorns’ three points were tied for their fewest against a Gwinnett County team since an 18-0 loss to Shiloh in 2021.
Much of that had to do with the stifling defense that Lamar-coached teams have become known for.
“We hang our hat on defense,” Lamar said. “Our guys fly around and get after it. We keep playing defense until you cross the goal line. That's always been our deal. We really don't flinch. We're going to make you keep snapping the ball. As long as we don't let you in the end zone, you have to keep fighting and we'll fight you all the way down to the 1-inch line. I told our guys when they got the field goal, we're not letting them in.”
A third-down drop and a 17-yard punt doomed Lanier’s season-opening drive, but South Gwinnett’s Didier Funez had his 41-yard field goal attempt blocked by Graham O’Kelley on the other end to keep the game scoreless.
After Lanier’s second three-and-out, Peoples helped engineer an eight-play, 73-yard scoring drive, stamped with his 1-yard rushing touchdown with 5:57 left in the first quarter.
The third Longhorn punt was followed with Peoples’ second touchdown, this time a 4-yard back-corner pass to Cohl Hendon, giving the Comets a 14-0 lead with 42 seconds remaining in the first.
“C.J.'s great,” Lamar said. “He does it the right way. We’ve got a lot of kids that got to learn how to do it the right way, but C.J. does it the right way. He challenges guys, he's consistent, he puts time in on the field, off the field. This is just a byproduct. He’s going to have a phenomenal year just because of his work. His preparation is unbelievable.”
Lanier pieced together its first positive, but was forced to settle for Noah Samples’ 26-yard field goal at the 3:57 mark of the second quarter.
With a chance to cut its deficit down further, Lanier continued to unravel. Jordan Alexander muffed a fair catch on his own 1-yard line and Thomas Morris ran in the third Comet touchdown just two plays later.
Despite committing 12 first-half penalties for 102 yards, South Gwinnett capitalized on even sloppier Lanier play to take a commanding 21-3 lead into halftime.
Trailing by 18 midway through the third and desperate for a spark, Lanier quarterback Dominic Larocca hit Isaiah Marshall for an apparent 51-yard reception, but Lanier’s 11th penalty of the game — this time a hold — extinguished the temporary flame.
The mistakes continued for Lanier, which turned the ball over on Larocca’s fumble, recovered by South at its 37-yard line.
After a perfectly placed punt by South Gwinnett’s Tristian Hayes was downed at the 1-yard line, linebacker Chris Frazier took Anthony Chaves down in the end zone for a safety, giving the Comets a 23-3 lead with 2:01 remaining in the third.
Thomas Morris put the finishing touches on the South Gwinnett blowout, rushing for a 3-yard score in the final minutes.
For a program eager to remove the bad taste that a losing season left last year, Lamar and company couldn’t have scripted a better start.
“We’ve got great kids, we've got a great community and we wanted to put them on the biggest stage,” Lamar said. “I'm just proud of how they showed up.”
